text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cancellation of controls on the movement of foreign currency. Forex dealers say it is a brave decision which shows the strength of the dinar and encourages trust in investment.
- Jordan and Israel set up a joint committee to remove obstacles to three-way trade between them and the Palestinians.
- Prosecution will wind up its case in military trial of Ahmed Daqamsa, who shot seven Israeli schoolgirls, on Saturday.
- Work expected to start soon on building American University in Red Sea port of Aqaba.
- Cabinet allows private sector to invest in electricity generation.

- Interior Minister Nazir Rasheed briefs regional governors on preparations for parliamentary elections. Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali affirms the importance of retaining Jordan's democratic image.
- National Constitutional Party, formed out of merger of nine small pro-government parties, aims at capturing 45 out of 80 parliamentary seats in elections.
- Four psychiatrists, testifying for defence, confirm that Ahmed Daqamsa is mentally ill.
- Higher council for investments to discuss today lifting the foreign share ownership ceiling to 70 percent from 50 percent.
- Israeli Trade Minister Natan Sharansky says Israel to facilitate movement of goods to West Bank.
- Jordan rejects Israeli security request at Aqaba airport.
